judged_by: Matched by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent on 2026-11-25; not yet checked by the labeler.

question.note: Spillover of the label/advertisement onto perceptions of people with records (Q1) and the effect on perceived representation (Q3); wording follows the paper's own question (p.4).

central_claim.note: Gives the ad's harm to perceptions and its improvement of representation; the counter-narrative part is in the next entry. Says 'advertisement with the label', the paper's wording, not the words alone (C-x3).
Counter-narrative part of C1. 'Substantially mitigated' matches the abstract's 'vastly ameliorated'; the quote gives the order (preceded by).

evidence.note: Survey experiment (E1, without sample/platform in the claim), the three arms (E2, without N), and stimuli: ad labeling Trump 'convicted criminal' and a counter-narrative about a formerly incarcerated state representative (E3 without the mugshot or the news-excerpt source).

Data source (Prolific, July 2025, self-identified Democrats in the U.S.; E1 without 'experiment', which is in entry 0, and without pre-registration) and total N of 2,439 (E2; arms are in entry 0). 2,439 is the final sample; the quote gives the 2,500 recruited.
Lists all six outcomes and that they are indices/Likert items; the item counts (five-item, two-item) are detail. Borderline match vs partial.

key_findings.note: Keeps 'before the advertisement' and 'relative to the advertisement alone'.

Both the representation and the public-service-motives increases, as the calibration judge credited. 'Suggesting a comparative benchmarking effect' is the author's hedged interpretation reported as a suggestion.

flags.text: Says system-impacted respondents were more positive 'across all items and treatment arms'; the paper says so 'with only one exception' (p.16), which the quote keeps but the claim drops.

key_findings.note: Main effect of system-impacted status is accurate but not gold; the larger ad effect for system-impacted respondents is part of F6 (the counter-narrative heterogeneity is not stated).

scope_and_limits.note: Durability, repeated exposure and behavior; the quote is the lead-in sentence but the claim states all three parts (p.17).
AI-generated responses as a concern for online panels, with the paper's own mitigation (Prolific's low rates).

theoretical_positioning.note: Reported as a suggestion ('suggesting ... may'), as the calibration judge credited.

interlocutor_claim.note: Refs 45-46 are Todd & Galinsky 2014 and Harney 2023; the incarcerated-individuals part is ref 47, a small attribution slip, not flagged.

flags.text: 'Using it to argue that the Democratic Party's stigmatizing strategy was counterproductive': the paper uses the meta-analysis to question negative ads and says stigmatizing terms were unnecessary and might backfire ('though this is also not guaranteed', p.3); it does not argue the strategy was counterproductive.
